Tech Stocks Fall on AI Concerns
 
Plus, Meta shares fall after it discloses further spending commitments and Treasury yields drop below 5%.
 
By Heard on the Street Staff
 
 
MICHAEL NAGLE/BLOOMBERG NEWS
 

This is an edition of the Markets P.M. newsletter, a recap of the day’s most important markets moves, delivered after the closing bell. If you’re not subscribed, sign up here.

 
 
 

What Happened in Markets Today

 

Meta Platforms shares fell 7% after the company disclosed additional billions of dollars in future spending commitments. In a Thursday filing, the company said it signed onto future leases and noncancelable contracts that added up to some $825 billion to support its AI buildout, up from nearly $700 million in commitments in July.

 

Oil prices surged, with Brent crude futures rising 4% to $133.17 a barrel after an attack on Saudi Arabia’s civilian airport. Saudi Arabia blamed Iran-backed Houthis for the attack. The U.S. military is said to be preparing a range of options to strike Iran.

 

Investors sold tech stocks and bought bonds. The Nasdaq fell 2.6% and AI growth-linked stocks fared the worst. CoreWeave and SpaceX fell 10% and 9%, respectively. Energy names were hit, too, with GE Vernova and Vistra falling 11% and 10%, respectively. The 10-year Treasury yield declined 0.193 percentage point to 4.952%. The S&P 500 fell 1.2% and the Dow was flat.

 

Moderna’s shares plunged 18%, making it the worst performer in the S&P 500, after details from a closely guarded mRNA-based cancer vaccine study were shared on social media. The results appeared largely positive, according to analysts, but still fell short of the market’s high expectations.

Mark Zuckerberg considered leaving California as a result of a proposed wealth tax that could force a share sale, which would have reduced his control over the company. Meta Platforms’ board cut him a deal to help keep him in the state.
